reach.rationale: Only long-stable APIs: classic Nuxt composables, file-based pages/server routes, and Vue 3.5's useId. No experimental flags, no vue-router 5 new APIs, no definePage or data loaders.

containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; the single new-ish surface (useId) is isolated to one component and all fetching goes through one wrapper composable.

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so there is nothing to justify; the code deliberately stays on the boring, documented path.

findings.issue: Pins nuxt ^4.6.2, but 4.6.3 (2026-10-27) shipped security fixes for versions >=4.6.0 (GHSA-9v7c-q64q-vv33 and related path-traversal advisories).
findings.suggestion: Bump to ^4.6.3; the app has no server middleware, so impact is minimal, but staying on the latest patch is cheap insurance.

findings.issue: router.options.scrollBehaviorType:'auto' restates the framework default; the option is stable (Nuxt >=3.7) but the line adds noise without effect.
findings.suggestion: Delete the router block, or keep it only if the team intends to switch to 'smooth' later.

findings.issue: Direct dependencies on vue ^3.5.44 and vue-router ^5.4.0 duplicate versions Nuxt already manages; vue-router 5 is a recent major (v5.0.0, 2026-01-29), so a stray caret bump could drift ahead of what Nuxt pins.
findings.suggestion: Drop the explicit vue/vue-router entries (or keep them matched to Nuxt's requirement) and let Nuxt own the router version; the app uses no vue-router 5-specific APIs.

summary: This app is deliberately boring in the best sense: it uses only long-stable Nuxt 4, Vue 3.5 and h3 APIs, with zero experimental flags, imports or markers. The one Nuxt-specific router option it sets restates the default, and the vue-router@5 pin merely mirrors what Nuxt 4.6.2 requires, with none of v5's experimental features (data loaders, definePage macros) in use. Risk of upstream churn breaking it is negligible; the only action items are a patch bump to nuxt 4.6.3 (security fixes) and removing redundant config.
